results.name: hard-task-model
replies: Session running: LRUCache implementation with O(1) operations and TTL support.

children.title: Implement LRUCache
children.brief:
Goal: Implement an LRUCache class in lru.js with O(1) get/put operations, capacity-based eviction using LRU order, and an optional ttlMs parameter where expired entries are never returned and are evicted on access. Write thorough tests covering eviction order, TTL expiration, edge cases, and all major operations.

Context: Create lru.js with the LRUCache implementation. The cache should:
- Accept capacity (max entries) and optional ttlMs (time-to-live in milliseconds) in the constructor
- get(key): return the value if present and not expired, return undefined otherwise; mark as recently used
- put(key, value): set or update an entry, mark as recently used; if at capacity, evict the least-recently-used entry
- has(key): return true if key exists and is not expired
- delete(key): remove an entry
- clear(): remove all entries
- size: property returning current number of entries
- Evicted entries should never be returned even if still in the cache
- When a key is accessed (get), it becomes most-recently used
- When a key is set (put), it becomes most-recently used

Constraints: O(1) time complexity for get/put operations is required. No external libraries beyond Node.js built-ins for the implementation.

Done when: lru.js exports LRUCache class, test file passes all tests including:
- Basic get/put operations and eviction order
- TTL expiration (entries expire and are never returned)
- Capacity eviction (LRU entry removed when capacity exceeded)
- Multiple access patterns and edge cases
- Tests verify O(1) performance characteristics

risks: Constructor signature is LRUCache(capacity, ttlMs) positional; the brief did not say whether ttlMs is positional or an options object, so I chose positional.
size counts expired entries that have not yet been accessed or evicted; get/has evict them lazily and they never get returned.
has() does not change recency order; the brief only specified get and put for recency.
put on an existing key refreshes its TTL.
Invalid capacity (non-positive-integer) or ttlMs (non-positive or non-finite) throws RangeError.
O(1) is verified by timing ratios (best of 3), which can be sensitive to a noisy machine; the threshold is a generous 4x.

checks.name: reply content
checks.detail: `let` declares a variable that can be reassigned; `const` declares one that can'

replies: `let` declares a variable that can be reassigned; `const` declares one that can't be. Both are block-scoped. With `const`, you can't rebind the reference, but if it holds an object or array, you can still mutate its contents—the immutability is shallow, not deep.
